ambition.goal_beyond: The cafes' Instagram keeps people interested in the coffee and the places, and stays that way without one person having to rescue it.

answers.question: What is the business and account?
answers.answer: Specialty coffee roaster with two cafes. Instagram 9,400 followers.

answers.question: What changed and when?
answers.answer: Engagement rate fell from about 4% to 1.8% over six months (Instagram insights, reported).

answers.question: How is posting run today?
answers.answer: Three staff post whenever they have time; no plan and no brand guide.

answers.question: What access exists?
answers.answer: Instagram access through Meta Business Suite with live access. Brand colours and logo files are in a Drive folder.

answers.question: Target, deadline, limits and who decides?
answers.answer: Engagement back to 3.5% and a consistent look within three months. No paid influencer deals. Keep data here. I decide with our cafe manager.

answers.question: My guess for what should happen after this (ambition)
answers.answer: Accepted as the working guess: you want Instagram to keep working without a rescue, so we aim for the causes and a routine, not only a one-off clean-up.

research.approach: Practitioners start from the post-by-post export, not the dashboard summary, and first pin down how engagement is counted, because dividing by followers, reach or views gives very different numbers and Instagram renamed impressions to views in 2025. They then split the fall by post type, day, topic and who posted, and check account-level causes such as follower quality and recommendation limits. Instagram ranks each surface separately (Feed, Stories, Reels, Explore) on early likes, comments, shares and saves, and on how often a viewer interacts with the account, so steady posting and content that invites a reply or share matter. Reels are shown to people who do not follow the account, and are shown less when they are low-resolution, watermarked or reposted. Brand consistency comes from a short guide (palette, logo use, photo style, caption voice) and templates the staff can reuse, then a weekly review of what worked. Public benchmarks measured per follower sit far below 3.5%, so the target needs a stated formula and an honest comparison.

sources.title: Instagram Ranking Explained (Adam Mosseri, Instagram)

steps.name: Write the brand guide from existing assets and the current feed
steps.why: A short guide with palette, logo use, photo style and voice is what lets three people post one look.

steps.name: Export post-by-post insights and rebuild the rate
steps.why: The raw per-post export shows what moved; a dashboard average hides it.

steps.name: Fix the engagement formula and check for tool changes
steps.why: The same account scores 0.5% or 4% depending on the divisor, and impressions became views in 2025.

steps.name: Split the fall by format, topic, day, poster and follower quality
steps.why: Each cause needs a different fix and several can act at once.

steps.name: Build the content system: pillars, formats, templates and a rota
steps.why: Steady posting on a few repeatable formats suits three busy staff and the way Instagram ranks interaction history.

steps.name: Schedule the first month, one change at a time
steps.why: Changes made in steps can be read; all at once they cannot.

steps.name: Review weekly on the same formula and learn
steps.why: A short weekly look catches a slide early and feeds the next plan.

pitfalls.text: Comparing rates that use different divisors (followers, reach, views), or before and after the views change, and calling it a fall or a win.
Chasing a reach spike from reposted or watermarked Reels, which Instagram shows less.
Changing look, format and posting rhythm all at once, so nothing can be credited.
Over-planning for three part-time staff so the plan is dropped in a month.

hypotheses.statement: The 4% and 1.8% are not the same formula, or the tool changed, so part of the fall is a counting change.
hypotheses.test: Recompute both periods from the export by followers, by reach and by views; compare with the reported figures.
hypotheses.confirm_if: One formula reproduces 4% earlier but a different one reproduces 1.8% now, or the two formulas move in opposite directions.
hypotheses.refute_if: The same formula gives close to 4% earlier and 1.8% now (within 0.2 points).

hypotheses.statement: The mix moved toward post types that earn less interaction.
hypotheses.test: Share of posts and median interactions per post by format (image, carousel, reel, story) before and after.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The weaker format's share of posts rose by 15 points or more while its median interactions are lower than another format's with at least 10 posts.
hypotheses.refute_if: The mix is stable, or moved toward the stronger format.

hypotheses.statement: Irregular posting weakens the account's interaction history with followers.
hypotheses.test: Posts per week and gaps in days between posts, before and after; compare engagement after long gaps.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Gaps of 7 days or more are more common since the fall, and posts after gaps earn less than the median.
hypotheses.refute_if: Rhythm is steady and posts after gaps do not earn less.

hypotheses.statement: Follower growth added people who never engage, which lowers a per-follower rate.
hypotheses.test: Follower growth by week against reach per follower and interactions per reach.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Followers grew while reach and interactions stayed flat or fell, so interactions per reach held but per-follower fell.
hypotheses.refute_if: Followers were flat and interactions per reach also fell.

hypotheses.statement: The content drifted from what earns interaction, and the messy look makes posts harder to recognise.
hypotheses.test: Tag topics and visual style for the top 10 and bottom 10 posts before and after; read comments and saves.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Top posts share a topic or style that is rare since the fall, and bottom posts are mostly off-pattern.
hypotheses.refute_if: Top and bottom posts show no topic or style pattern.

hypotheses.statement: Reach fell because of reel quality or account limits (reposted, watermarked or low-quality reels, or a recommendation limit).
hypotheses.test: Check account status in Instagram; compare reach for reels with and without those traits.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Account status shows a limit, or reels with those traits have clearly lower reach.
hypotheses.refute_if: No limit shows and reels with those traits reach about as many people.

measurement.window: Weekly for 12 weeks from the first scheduled post, compared with the 12 weeks before on the same formula.
measurement.min_volume: At least 10 posts per format before calling a format better; at least 4 weeks before calling the overall rate changed.
measurement.stop_rule: Pause a change and review if median reach or follower count falls for two weeks in a row; otherwise run the full window.
